correctness.summary: Equality of all upper-diagonal moments gives equality, for every q>=0, of the circle pushforwards of |z|^(2q) mu and of z|z|^(2q) mu by psi(z)=z/bar(z), because their Fourier coefficients are the moments with total degree 2q and 2q+1. Disintegration over the common angular pushforward reduces equality to each finite psi-fiber. Vandermonde inversion recovers the total mass at each distinct squared radius, and the z-weighted moments then separate the at-most-two antipodal points at a fixed radius. For an algebraic zero set avoiding 0, restriction of p(z,bar z) to any radial line is a nonzero one-variable polynomial since p(0,0) != 0, so every ray fiber is finite. Combining this injectivity with Theorem 22(i)-(ii) of the source gives the stated bijection and determinacy consequences.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2019 source explicitly assumes injectivity of psi_p for its strongest algebraic-support conclusions and leaves the singleton-PDE converse open in general. Its own examples note that standard algebraic curves and polynomial automorphisms can violate that injectivity. Searches by title, DOI, PDE(gamma), upper-diagonal positive-definite extension, algebraic support, finite fibers/radial intersections, and the cited hyperbola/parabola geometry did not locate a result replacing one-point radial intersections by finite intersections or removing psi_p injectivity for every algebraic zero set avoiding 0. A 2020 survey discusses the paper without this strengthening, while a 2025 dynamic-inverse complex-moment paper addresses a different moment formulation. Differently phrased, unpublished, or poorly indexed prior coverage remains possible.

value.summary: The result removes the restrictive geometric hypothesis from the full algebraic-support class away from the origin, upgrading a named partial solution of an open determinacy question. It also gives a reusable finite-fiber separation principle: even and odd upper-diagonal levels jointly recover conditional radial masses and antipodal signs.

limitations: The general implication PDE(gamma) singleton => gamma determinate remains open outside the finite-ray setting.
The algebraic corollary assumes the algebraic zero set avoids the origin.
Supports with an infinite radial fiber, such as a radial-line component, are not covered.
The argument is qualitative and gives no stability estimate under perturbation of moments.
A differently phrased, unpublished, or poorly indexed prior result may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.
